metadata.title: Premarket movers: Palo Alto soars, chip stocks rally ahead of Anthropic debut

content.text:
Investing.com -- U.S. equity futures jumped early Thursday after Anthropic's initial public offering priced above expectations, reviving enthusiasm for artificial intelligence stocks. Dow Jones Industrial Average futures rose 0.6%, S&P 500 futures gained 1.2% and Nasdaq-100 futures surged 2.1%.
The company behind Claude is set to debut on the Nasdaq on Thursday under the ticker ANT. It priced the largest initial public offering on record, boosting confidence in the AI trade. The deal values Anthropic at about $1.5 trillion on a fully diluted basis.
The pricing lifted the broader tech and chip sector. Nvidia rose 1.5% and AMD gained 2.9% by 07:36 ET (12:36 GMT). Micron Technology climbed 4.8% and SK Hynix's American depositary receipts rose 5.3%. Intel, Marvell, Lam Research and Applied Materials each added more than 4%.
Palo Alto Networks shares surged nearly 10% after the company raised its annual revenue forecast and agreed to acquire AI startup Applied Compute for $4.5 billion. The company said a heightened threat environment is pushing customers toward broader security products.
Palo Alto now expects fiscal 2027 revenue of $14.52 billion to $14.57 billion, up from its prior forecast of $14.10 billion to $14.20 billion. The move sparked a wider rally in cybersecurity stocks, with CrowdStrike, Okta, Zscaler and Rubrik all trading higher.
Elsewhere, PDD Holdings, the owner of Temu, rose more than 7% after the China-based e-commerce company beat Wall Street estimates for third-quarter adjusted profit. The company cut spending on sales and marketing.
Meanwhile, Warner Music Group shares slipped over 4% following its latest quarterly results.
